accent.note: Resolved 2.8.5. Was #45D6B8 in /shared and Compose while Windows, the README badges and every release asset shipped #4ADFBF, plus a third hardcoded copy in MainWindow.ThemeBrush. Settled on the value users had actually seen; /shared changed first, both clients follow, the private fallback table deleted.

accent-brand.note: Now identical to accent. The name survives because the brand assets refer to it, not because it is a second colour.

light-accent.note: Darkened from #17A98C so white labels reach ~5.3:1 instead of ~3.0:1.

display.purpose: The one number or headline a screen is about.

pairing-code.purpose: The two digits the PC needs; tabular numerals, widely tracked so they cannot be misread.

win-code.purpose: The manual code field, Cascadia Mono at 25px with +150 character spacing.

win-caption.purpose: Status chip and column headers; tracking goes positive so it does not clot.

persianTypeface.incumbent: None bundled. shared/design-tokens.json declares typography.family.persian = 'Vazirmatn', but no font file exists in either app and no code path loads it; Persian renders in the platform system face today.
persianTypeface.decidedTarget: Estedad (aminabedi68/Estedad, OFL-1.1, variable, Arabic + Latin) - DECIDED, NOT YET IMPLEMENTED.

elevation.name: glass-rest
elevation.purpose: The material at rest. No shadow exists in this system.

elevation.name: glass-raised
elevation.purpose: The surface that is currently the subject.

elevation.name: glass-solid-fallback
elevation.purpose: Windows: the opaque stand-in when transparency effects are off. Darker than the scrim so foreground pairs keep contrast.

motion.name: spring-snappy
motion.purpose: Direct-manipulation feedback; button dips to scale 0.97 on pointer-down.

motion.name: spring-gentle
motion.purpose: Larger surfaces that feel frantic at standard rate.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: SystemPreferences.AnimationsEnabled == false becomes an instant state change
motion.purpose: Reduced motion is a code path, not a tuning.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one thing to do on this screen. Exactly one per screen.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #4ADFBF; color: #05201B; border: none; border-radius: 24px; height: 46px; width: 100%; font-family: 'Segoe UI Variable Text', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14.5px; font-weight: 600; transition: filter 0.15s, transform 0.12s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.08); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); filter: brightness(0.92); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid rgba(74,223,191,0.8); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The way out, or the lesser of two paths. Visibly recessive.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.12); color: rgba(255,255,255,0.96); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.18); border-radius: 24px; height: 46px; width: 100%; font-family: 'Segoe UI Variable Text', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14.5px; font-weight: 400; transition: background 0.15s, transform 0.12s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.2); } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid rgba(74,223,191,0.8); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Quiet Button
components.description: Text-weight action with no fill, so it cannot compete with the other two roles.
components.css: .ds-btn-quiet { background: transparent; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.72); border: none; border-radius: 24px; height: 44px; font-family: 'Segoe UI Variable Text', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 400; transition: color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-quiet:hover { color: rgba(255,255,255,0.96); } .ds-btn-quiet:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid rgba(74,223,191,0.8); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: Dot plus word. Colour reinforces the label; it never carries state alone.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.05); border-radius: 24px; padding: 5px 12px 5px 10px; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.36); font-family: 'Segoe UI Variable Text', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11.5px; letter-spacing: 0.012em; } .ds-chip-dot { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: #4ADFBF; }

components.name: Code Field
components.description: Two characters wide because the phone shows two digits. Validates on every keystroke; a valid code connects with no click.
components.css: .ds-input-code { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.08); color: rgba(255,255,255,0.96); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.18); border-radius: 12px; height: 64px; width: 100%; text-align: center; font-family: 'Cascadia Mono', Consolas, monospace; font-size: 25px; letter-spacing: 0.15em; transition: border-color 0.15s; } .ds-input-code::placeholder { color: rgba(255,255,255,0.36); } .ds-input-code:focus { outline: none; border-color: rgba(74,223,191,0.8); }

components.name: Glass Panel
components.description: The material itself: translucent fill, light-from-above gradient, specular top edge. No shadow.
components.css: .ds-glass { position: relative; border-radius: 24px; padding: 16px; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.96); background: linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.09), rgba(255,255,255,0.06)); font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; line-height: 22px; } .ds-glass::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 24px; padding: 1px; background: linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(255,255,255,0.22), rgba(255,255,255,0.12) 40%, rgba(255,255,255,0.12)); -webkit-mask: linear-gradient(#000 0 0) content-box, linear-gradient(#000 0 0); -webkit-mask-composite: xor; mask-composite: exclude; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Caption Button
components.description: Minimise and close. The deliberate exception to the 44px target rule - pointer-only affordances on a pointer-only surface.
components.css: .ds-btn-caption { background: transparent; border: none; border-radius: 7px; width: 32px; height: 28px; padding: 0; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.54); font-size: 11px; transition: background 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-caption:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.12); color: rgba(255,255,255,0.96); } .ds-btn-caption:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid rgba(74,223,191,0.8); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview: Relay's interface is a single translucent pane held over a deep, near-black field, with exactly one colour alive on it. The material does the work that shadows usually do: depth is communicated by translucency, a light-from-above gradient fill and a specular top edge, never by a hard drop shadow. The personality is deferent and quiet - state is the content, and everything else recedes behind it. The two implementations speak their own platform's dialect of the same material: Android carries a full dark and light glass set; the Windows tray popover is deliberately dark-only, because it floats over an arbitrary wallpaper and must read as one consistent object.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first, near-monochrome; colour carried almost entirely by alpha over white or black.
One teal accent, reserved for the single most important interactive thing on screen.
Depth from translucency and a 1px gradient stroke; no drop shadows anywhere.
4pt spacing grid; concentric radii (child radius = parent radius minus padding).
Spring motion described by response and damping ratio, never hand-picked durations.
Contrast always beats the glass effect - several token alphas exist at their current values because the prettier value failed AA.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: One accent per screen. If two elements on a screen are accented, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The No Nested Glass Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one glass layer. Nothing drawn on it is translucent over anything else.

rules.name: The Contrast-Wins Rule
rules.body: Legibility beats translucency, every time. Dark tertiary text sits at 60% alpha, light tertiary at 62%, and the light accent is #0F7A63 - these are the AA floor made visible, and as of 2.8.5 they are the values in /shared rather than a local Android correction the contract disagreed with. Do not restore the prettier values.

rules.name: The Redundant-Channel Rule
rules.body: Colour is never the only carrier of state. The status chip pairs its dot with the word.

rules.name: The Optical-Size Rule
rules.body: Large text uses the Display cut and small text the Text cut; tracking goes negative as size grows and positive as it shrinks.

rules.name: The Two-Digit Rule
rules.body: The manual code field is two characters wide because the phone shows two digits.

rules.name: The Flat-Material Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow, ever. If something needs to feel lifted, raise its fill alpha and let the stroke highlight do the rest.

rules.name: The One Glass Rule
rules.body: One translucent layer per app. Everything on it is opaque enough to read over an arbitrary backdrop.

rules.name: The Reduced-Motion Rule
rules.body: The system animation-effects switch is a code path, not a preference to read and ignore: with it off, every animation becomes an instant state change.

rules.name: The Concentricity Rule
rules.body: A child's radius is the parent's radius minus the padding between them, so curves stay parallel instead of drifting.

dos: Do change shared/design-tokens.json first. Both apps map it to platform constructs and both are asserted against /shared.
Do give exactly one element per screen the accent.
Do pair colour with a word or shape whenever it carries state.
Do keep the concentricity relationship when nesting: child radius = parent radius minus padding.
Do describe motion as response + damping ratio, and start every animation from the property's current value.
Do honour reduced motion as a branch, not a tuning.
Do keep every interactive target at 44px or larger, with 46px as the button height.
Do provide a solid fallback for any glass surface, darker than its scrim.
Do design RTL as a mirror, and pin flow direction on anything that is content rather than UI (camera frames).
donts: Don't add a box-shadow. Elevation is translucency in this system.
Don't nest glass on glass. There is one translucent layer per app.
Don't accent two things on one screen.
Don't lower the tertiary-text alphas or lighten the light-mode accent back toward their prettier originals - those exact values are what clears 4.5:1.
Don't let translucency win an argument against legibility.
Don't introduce a light theme for the Windows popover; it is dark-only on purpose.
Don't describe Estedad as the Persian face in use. It is the decided target; the system face is what renders today.
Don't add a fourth button role, or give two roles the same visual weight.
Don't introduce any surface that implies an account, a paid tier, or an upgrade - commercialization is an open decision and the product is free and open source today.
